entries.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
entries.description: The built-in engine. 25 European languages, punctuation + casing, word timestamps; the only model with a Qualcomm NPU path.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64, idle
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 --backend cpu --languages en,es,ru,uk`, 2026-09-18, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy decoding, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Token-weighted WER 0.054, warm RTF 0.0401, over 12 clip(s) in en/es/ru/uk. ONE SWEEP: every entry in this catalog was measured back to back on the CPU on this date, over the same committed fixture set, so the figures are comparable with each other. The CPU is the only accelerator they can all use -- sherpa-onnx links its own static ONNX Runtime with the CPU provider, so nothing but parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 has any other path. CLIP BASIS: a model is run only on the languages it claims; clips in other languages are SKIPPED rather than transcribed and discarded, so this RTF describes work on audio the model is actually for. WARM RTF, NOT THE ALL-CLIP MEAN: this is the mean over every clip AFTER the first, which is the same quantity the app records and shows under "on your machine". The first clip carries one-time session warm-up and is reported separately by `lw bench` as the cold RTF; on this sweep it ran 10-50% slower than the warm figure. An earlier revision of this catalog recorded the all-clip mean instead, which is a different quantity and made the two columns look like they disagreed. MEDIAN OF THREE back-to-back runs (0.0642, 0.0401, 0.0383). The error rate was identical in all three -- decoding is greedy and deterministic -- and the RTF was not. MACHINE STATE MATTERS AND IS RECORDED: this sweep was taken with the machine idle (CPU load 2-6%, app closed) and the run-to-run spread was 2-8%. The revision before it was taken while the machine was busy with an IDE, a browser, a sync client and compiler jobs; its spread reached 59% and its figures were 20-40% higher for every sherpa entry. Those were withdrawn, not adjusted. RTF here is still best read as a rank between these eight entries rather than an absolute for the silicon. The first of the three runs produced 0.0642, well outside the other two, which is ONNX Runtime's own session and thread-pool warm-up showing up beyond the single cold clip; the median discards it.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: docs/benchmarks.md 5.1 - `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --backend npu`, encoder on Hexagon HTP V81, 12 FLEURS clips, 2026-08-26

entries.notes: MEASURED on this project's target machine (Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E94100): end-to-end RTF 0.032 on the CPU EP and 0.0145 with the encoder on the Hexagon HTP V81, word-weighted WER 5.4% / 4.8% over 12 FLEURS clips - see docs/benchmarks.md 5.1. The per-language wer_estimates come from the same run with only 3 clips per language, so treat them as indicative, not statistically meaningful; the English figure is dominated by FLEURS number-word and casing normalisation ('2' vs 'two'), not misrecognition. download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact pinned file sizes in models/manifests/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.json and cover the CPU int8 artifact set, which is the only hash-pinned target today. The NPU path additionally needs a static-shape encoder and builds a ~1.2 GB HTP context binary locally on first use (~106 s, cached thereafter) - that is generated on the machine, not downloaded, and is not counted in disk_bytes. GPU: the same file also runs on a GPU through ONNX Runtime's WebGPU provider - no separate artifact and no extra download - measured on the X2's integrated Adreno at RTF 0.0862, WER 4.8% over the same 12 clips. The hardware field below lists artifact targets (which pinned file sets exist), not every provider that can run them. SPEED TIER CORRECTED 2026-09-18, from very_fast to fast, by measurement rather than by editorial judgement. Its warm CPU RTF is 0.0401; the four entries still marked very_fast measure 0.0099 to 0.0149, and omnilingual-300m -- already marked fast -- measures 0.0297. This entry sits with the second group, not the first. The tier is the input to the RTF estimate, so leaving it where it was would have made the estimate for its NPU path about three times too optimistic once the tiers were calibrated against real numbers. Nothing about the model changed; only the label describing its speed, which had been assigned before it was measured end to end.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/parakeet-tdt-ctc-110m-en.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. LICENCE: CC-BY-4.0, declared on the upstream model card nvidia/parakeet-tdt_ctc-110m. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16 - read the measurement's source line before quoting it. WHY A LANGUAGE SUBSET: `lw bench` scores only the clips in languages the engine claims, but lw-engine-sherpa reports a whole-family language list for offline transducers (the 25 European languages of the multilingual NeMo releases), which this monolingual export does not speak. Left to the full 12-clip set it would have been scored against Spanish, Russian and Ukrainian as well, producing a WER that describes nothing. So the run used a copy of tests/fixtures/audio holding only the English clips and their fixtures.json entries; the audio and the reference transcripts are the repository's own, unmodified. WHAT IT IS: NVIDIA's parakeet-tdt_ctc-110m is a hybrid trained with both a TDT-transducer and a CTC head on 36k hours of English; sherpa-onnx's conversion script (scripts/nemo/fast-conformer-hybrid-transducer-ctc/run-transducer-non-streaming.sh) exports the transducer branch, which is what is pinned here. It keeps punctuation and casing, like the 0.6B Parakeets. FULL PRECISION, NOT INT8: this is the one new entry whose artifact target is `any` rather than `cpu_int8`, because the matching csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet_tdt_transducer_110m-en-36000-int8 repository is empty apart from .gitattributes - the quantized files exist only inside the .tar.bz2 on the GitHub release, which the installer cannot unpack. That is why a 110M-parameter model costs 455 MiB to download while the 600M parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-en int8 costs 631 MiB. wer_estimates is empty: NVIDIA publishes figures for its own NeMo checkpoint, not for this ONNX export. Quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL; 'better' rather than 'best' places it below the 0.6B Parakeets on parameter count. The engine string is `nemo_transducer`, as on parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-en. In this catalog that string means 'the sherpa-onnx offline transducer loader' - the encoder/decoder/joiner/tokens.txt layout - not a claim about who trained the weights. It is deliberately not `parakeet_tdt`: the built-in parakeet_tdt engine only loads the istupakov file layout (nemo128.onnx + vocab.txt + a fused decoder_joint graph) and cannot read this triple, so labelling it parakeet_tdt would promise a path that does not exist. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Whisper large-v3-turbo (sherpa-onnx export)

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/whisper-turbo.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16: WER 0.042 over the same 12 clips on which whisper-medium scored 0.054 and parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 scored 0.054, at RTF 0.469 against medium's 1.250. On this fixture set that is the best accuracy-per-second of any Whisper entry here, but 12 clips cannot settle an ordering - read the source line before quoting it. wer_estimates stays empty for the usual reason: OpenAI's published figures describe the full-precision checkpoint, not this int8 export. Quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL. WHAT TURBO IS: large-v3's encoder with the decoder cut from 32 layers to 4 - not a smaller, weaker large, but large-v3's acoustic model with a cheap decoder; OpenAI documents it as degrading on some languages relative to large-v3 itself. The language list is therefore large-v3's: openai/whisper tokenizer.py LANGUAGES plus 'yue', which large-v3 is the first size to support and which turbo inherits with the same tokenizer. Only the int8 encoder/decoder pair is pinned; the full-precision graphs sit in the same upstream repository and would cost several times the download for a quality difference nobody here has measured. LICENCE NOTE: recorded as MIT, the licence of the openai/whisper repository whose original checkpoints sherpa-onnx's export script downloads and converts; the `openai/whisper-*` model cards on Hugging Face declare apache-2.0 instead, so read both before redistributing. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature. CHINESE, measured 2026-09-18 with `--languages zh` over the three FLEURS cmn_Hans clips, scored by CHARACTER error rate because Chinese is written without word delimiters, and taken as the median of three back-to-back runs: CER 0.380 at warm RTF 0.2126 -- the WORST Chinese of the four entries here that claim it, and by a distance: 2.7x sense-voice-small's 0.141 at 20x the real-time factor. That is worth stating plainly next to the `universal` role this entry holds, because the role is earned on en/es/ru/uk and does not extend to Chinese: a user who picks whisper-turbo for its coverage and then dictates Chinese gets the weakest option in the catalog. Kept out of the blended total above rather than folded into it -- a word rate and a character rate are different quantities. The character rate was identical in all three runs; only the RTF moved.

entries.description: Russian-only Conformer transducer from Sber's GigaChat team, exported for sherpa-onnx with punctuation and text normalisation built in.
entries.notes: MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-17: WER 0.029 at RTF 0.0175 over the three Russian FLEURS fixtures, against parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3's 0.059 on the same three clips - twice the accuracy at roughly half the real-time factor, in a third of the download. That RTF is from 2026-09-17 and is NOT the one to compare against the rest of this catalog; the comparable figure is in `measurements` below, re-measured on 2026-09-18 in one sweep with every other entry. entries.name: SenseVoice Small (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Alibaba's non-autoregressive multilingual model: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Cantonese in one pass, with inverse text normalisation and punctuation.
entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the two pinned file sizes in models/manifests/sense-voice-small.json (model.int8.onnx + tokens.txt); both SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes, because upstream publishes none. SOURCE: the `asr-models` GitHub release only ships .tar.bz2 archives, which the installer could not unpack when this entry was written, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. The installer gained archive support on 2026-09-18; this entry was deliberately left on the loose files, because those hashes are the ones that were verified locally and re-pinning to the archive would discard that verification for no gain. LICENCE - READ THIS: not an SPDX licence. The export repository's LICENSE file points at the FunASR Model Open Source License Agreement v1.1 (https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR/blob/main/MODEL_LICENSE), a custom Alibaba Group agreement which permits use, copying, modification and sharing but requires attribution and retention of model names, disclaims all liability, and terminates if you 'denigrate' the software. It is not OSI-approved and is more restrictive than the MIT/CC-BY terms of the other entries; check it before redistributing. MEASURED SINCE: this paragraph used to read 'no run of any kind on any machine'. It has since been run twice on the target machine - the comparable CPU sweep recorded in `measurements` below, and the Chinese character-rate run described at the end of this note. wer_estimates is still empty: FunAudioLLM publishes comparisons against Whisper on AISHELL-1/Common Voice for the full-precision checkpoint, not for this int8 ONNX export, and we did not retrieve that table. The quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL; 'very_fast' reflects that SenseVoice Small is non-autoregressive (one encoder pass, no token-by-token decode loop), not a timing. The engine string is `sense_voice`, which this build's EngineKind does not know - it round-trips as an unknown engine, which is intended for a catalog that may outlive the binary. CHINESE, measured 2026-09-18 with `--languages zh` over the three FLEURS cmn_Hans clips added that day, scored by CHARACTER error rate because Chinese is written without word delimiters: CER 0.141 at warm RTF 0.0109 -- the best Chinese in this catalog, from the smallest and fastest of the three that claim it. Kept out of the blended total above rather than folded into it -- a word rate and a character rate are different quantities. Three clips is a small sample and one of them (fleurs_zh_2) embeds a Latin word in parentheses, which every model here stumbles on; the ranking between them is worth more than any single figure. For comparison on the same three clips, each the warm RTF and the median of three back-to-back runs on an idle machine: sense-voice-small CER 0.141 at 0.0109, qwen3-asr-0.6b 0.155 at 0.0924, omnilingual-300m 0.310 at 0.0292, whisper-turbo 0.380 at 0.2126. The character rates were identical in every run; only the RTFs moved.

entries.name: Qwen3-ASR 0.6B (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Alibaba's LLM-style speech recogniser: a convolutional frontend and encoder feeding a Qwen decoder, covering 30 languages including Chinese, Russian and English.
entries.notes: MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-18, and the result is split enough to be worth stating per language rather than as one figure: en 0.031, es 0.024, ru 0.206 over three clips each. That makes it the joint best English in this catalog -- it ties whisper-turbo's 0.031 at well under half the real-time factor, 0.1162 against 0.2551 -- and the worst Russian of anything here that claims Russian, 3.5x parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3's 0.059 and 7x gigaam-v3-ru's 0.029. It therefore carries NO role: `accurate` would be read as a general claim, and on the languages this fixture set can actually score, whisper-turbo matches or beats it everywhere. Its place here is coverage -- 30 languages plus 22 Chinese dialects, including Chinese, Japanese and Korean -- and part of that coverage is now measured: the Chinese fixtures and the character error rate this note asked for were both added on 2026-09-18, and the result is in the CHINESE paragraph below. Japanese, Korean and Cantonese are still unmeasured - there are no fixtures for them - so the 30-language claim remains mostly untested by this project. FIRST ARCHIVE ENTRY: published only as a .tar.bz2 on the sherpa-onnx release with no loose-file mirror, so the manifest pins the ARCHIVE's SHA-256 and the installer unpacks it only after that hash matches (see crates/lw-core/src/model/archive.rs). download_bytes is the archive; disk_bytes is what is kept -- the test audio, README and shell scripts in the archive are not written. VERIFIED: the SHA-256 was computed locally from the bytes downloaded, and the whole path was exercised by a real `lw models install`. LICENCE: Apache-2.0, from the Qwen/Qwen3-ASR-* model cards; the sherpa-onnx export script is Apache-2.0 too. LANGUAGES: the thirty the card names, NOT Ukrainian -- an earlier draft of the language table wrongly added it, which would have scored this model against the Ukrainian fixtures and reported 0.852 as its accuracy. SIZE: 838 MiB down and 941 MiB on disk, the largest entry here by a distance; the decoder alone is 756 MB, which is what an LLM decoder costs even at int8. CHINESE, measured 2026-09-18 with `--languages zh` over the three FLEURS cmn_Hans clips added that day, scored by CHARACTER error rate because Chinese is written without word delimiters: CER 0.155 at warm RTF 0.0924 -- close to SenseVoice on accuracy, six times slower and nearly four times the download. Kept out of the blended total above rather than folded into it -- a word rate and a character rate are different quantities. Three clips is a small sample and one of them (fleurs_zh_2) embeds a Latin word in parentheses, which every model here stumbles on; the ranking between them is worth more than any single figure. For comparison on the same three clips, each the warm RTF and the median of three back-to-back runs on an idle machine: sense-voice-small CER 0.141 at 0.0109, qwen3-asr-0.6b 0.155 at 0.0924, omnilingual-300m 0.310 at 0.0292, whisper-turbo 0.380 at 0.2126. The character rates were identical in every run; only the RTFs moved.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64, idle
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/qwen3-asr-0.6b --backend cpu --languages en,es,ru,uk`, 2026-09-18, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy decoding, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Token-weighted WER 0.071, warm RTF 0.0901, over 9 clip(s) in en/es/ru. ONE SWEEP: every entry in this catalog was measured back to back on the CPU on this date, over the same committed fixture set, so the figures are comparable with each other. The CPU is the only accelerator they can all use -- sherpa-onnx links its own static ONNX Runtime with the CPU provider, so nothing but parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 has any other path. CLIP BASIS: a model is run only on the languages it claims; clips in other languages are SKIPPED rather than transcribed and discarded, so this RTF describes work on audio the model is actually for. WARM RTF, NOT THE ALL-CLIP MEAN: this is the mean over every clip AFTER the first, which is the same quantity the app records and shows under "on your machine". The first clip carries one-time session warm-up and is reported separately by `lw bench` as the cold RTF; on this sweep it ran 10-50% slower than the warm figure. An earlier revision of this catalog recorded the all-clip mean instead, which is a different quantity and made the two columns look like they disagreed. MEDIAN OF THREE back-to-back runs (0.0973, 0.0901, 0.0895). The error rate was identical in all three -- decoding is greedy and deterministic -- and the RTF was not. MACHINE STATE MATTERS AND IS RECORDED: this sweep was taken with the machine idle (CPU load 2-6%, app closed) and the run-to-run spread was 2-8%. The revision before it was taken while the machine was busy with an IDE, a browser, a sync client and compiler jobs; its spread reached 59% and its figures were 20-40% higher for every sherpa entry. Those were withdrawn, not adjusted. RTF here is still best read as a rank between these eight entries rather than an absolute for the silicon. The three Ukrainian clips were skipped because this model does not claim Ukrainian; an earlier draft of the language table wrongly added it, which would have scored 0.852 against it here.

entries.name: Omnilingual ASR 300M CTC v2 (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Meta's 1600-language CTC recogniser, the compact 300M member of the family, in 279 MiB.
entries.notes: MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-18, and the measurement CONTRADICTED the reason it was added. It was picked as a likely `universal` role holder - 1600 languages in a quarter of whisper-turbo's download - and on the four languages this fixture set can score it is the weakest entry in the catalog: en 0.185 against moonshine-tiny's 0.092 and qwen3's 0.031, ru 0.088 against gigaam's 0.029, uk 0.296 against parakeet's 0.074. Only Spanish (0.024) is competitive. whisper-turbo keeps the `universal` role on 0.042 across the same clips; this entry carries NO role. WHY IT IS STILL HERE: coverage nothing else offers. 279 MiB for the long tail - a user whose language appears in no other entry has an option instead of nothing, and 'worse than a specialist' beats 'not supported'. Choose it for a language nothing else claims, not for a language something else does. LANGUAGES: upstream claims 1600+; the 103 listed are the COMPUTED intersection of Meta's own per_language_results_table_7B_llm_asr.csv (1683 rows) with this project's language-name table - every code was checked to be in that file, none assumed. The other ~1580 are real and omitted only because this program can neither name nor score them. META'S OWN FIGURES, for the 7B LLM model and NOT this 300M CTC one, as CER: ru 1.5, es 1.3, de 1.5, uk 2.1, en 3.0 - but zh 11.5, yue 17.0, ja 19.2. The gap between those and what was measured here is the gap between a 7B LLM decoder and a 300M CTC head; do not quote the CSV as this entry's accuracy. NOT FOR CHINESE on either model's numbers. LICENCE: Apache-2.0, read from the LICENSE file in the archive (Copyright 2025 Meta Platforms). ARCHIVE entry: the archive's SHA-256 is pinned and it is unpacked only after that matches; the test audio and README are not written to the model directory. CHINESE, measured 2026-09-18 with `--languages zh` over the three FLEURS cmn_Hans clips added that day, scored by CHARACTER error rate because Chinese is written without word delimiters: CER 0.310 at warm RTF 0.0292 -- twice the error of the other two, as Meta's own zh figure predicted. Kept out of the blended total above rather than folded into it -- a word rate and a character rate are different quantities. Three clips is a small sample and one of them (fleurs_zh_2) embeds a Latin word in parentheses, which every model here stumbles on; the ranking between them is worth more than any single figure. For comparison on the same three clips, each the warm RTF and the median of three back-to-back runs on an idle machine: sense-voice-small CER 0.141 at 0.0109, qwen3-asr-0.6b 0.155 at 0.0924, omnilingual-300m 0.310 at 0.0292, whisper-turbo 0.380 at 0.2126. The character rates were identical in every run; only the RTFs moved.
